svg.title: Escape Room Adventure | Templates and complete save state

g.text: Escape Room Adventure | Templates and complete save state
Leading zeroes and internal characters stay significant.
Each room defines its objects, actions, one optional successor and two gates.
Starting at startingRoomId, successors visit EVERY room exactly once
and end at an empty nextRoomId. No broken references, self-loops,
cycles, branching, unreachable rooms or backward navigation are allowed.
Item requirements must be obtainable here or earlier on that path,
without passing either gate of the room that requires them.
Room authors make required items appear before they can be left behind.
Each Action.appearingItemIds set is immutable and names its own room's items.
Objects have no lock field; they complete their own actions.
ItemLockDefinition requires a nonempty set of configured item IDs.
All items are instantiated in ROOM at their configured roomId.
New-game construction enters only the starting room before publication,
auto-acquiring its initiallyRevealed items; future-room visible items stay ROOM.
Factory instantiates independent mutable runtime rooms/items/locks.
New TEMPLATE Trivia requires an authored initial question;
new API Trivia starts uninitialized and is fetched on demand.
Restored API Trivia reuses the retained saved question.
Conditions/effects and text configuration are immutable values.
Remaining definition fields are specified in escape-room-class-diagram.md.
Every configured item has exactly one authoritative location:
ROOM = its configured owning room; INVENTORY = Inventory.
roomId exists exactly for ROOM and must match the configured owner.
INVENTORY items have no roomId and must be revealed.
Successful action appearances and first entry transfer the SAME items
ROOM -> INVENTORY and set revealed=true. Already-held IDs are skipped.
Hidden ROOM items may remain false; unentered visible ROOM items may be true.
Actions and door checks leave held items in inventory.
No separate inventory list duplicates these saved locations.
create generates values once, resolving descriptions/results
and authored answers consistently into independent worlds.
The new-game Game constructor calls private enterRoom(startingRoomId),
preflighting all visible-item transfers before publishing the world.
Start names the resulting brand-new inventory once in its initial message.
restore requires schema 4 and compatible template ID/version.
Rebuild successor structure from that matching immutable template.
Increment template.version whenever successors or appearance rules change;
Reject previous schemas without migration. Validate complete global
ID coverage, item locations, object values/one-shot action IDs,
two room-owned locks per room and all generated values.
An unlocked ItemLock requires ALL its requiredItemIds in INVENTORY.
A locked door with every required item held remains valid:
unlocking requires an explicit command, not automatic inference.
Preserve both gates in either completion order.
Validate lock subtype/question compatibility and current room/status.
Every predecessor of the saved current room must have BOTH gates passed;
current-room gates remain independent and may be incomplete.
An unreachable saved position is invalid;
ESCAPED requires currentRoom.nextRoomId empty and both gates passed.
Reconstruct a separate candidate through validated constructors.
Restore replays NO action and performs NO API call or RNG.
The state constructor restores saved locations exactly: no enterRoom,
automatic acquisition, duplicate item or replayed obtained notification.
Only a completely validated candidate replaces the context.
Save exactly every room's door ItemLock and exit TriviaLock.
Retain the original question and expected answer for initialized Trivia.
ItemLock has no question; an unlocked TriviaLock must retain one.
TEMPLATE questions must match the template resolved with saved values.
API questions retain their original saved content without fetching.
Snapshot includes hidden items and state from unvisited rooms.
Schema 4 values are unchanged: no successor list or final-room flag is saved.
Appearance rules stay in the template; no acquisition ledger is saved.
Description text is derived from restored object state and template.
Expected answers never enter application display data.
One manual save: injected Path, default data/savegame.json.
Write and close a same-directory temp file, then atomically replace.
On failure preserve the previous save; clean up the temporary file.
Unsupported atomic replacement is a reported save failure.
use-case-owned DataAccessException. JSON/HTTP/Path stay in adapters.
captures all rooms and item containers
